# AGENTS.md — Tolaria Vault

This is a [Tolaria](https://github.com/refactoringhq/tolaria) vault: a folder of Markdown files with YAML frontmatter forming a personal knowledge graph.

Keep edits compatible with Tolaria's current conventions. Prefer small, human-readable changes over heavy restructuring.

## Core conventions

- One Markdown note per file.
- The first H1 in the body is the preferred display title.
- Legacy `title:` frontmatter is still read as a fallback when a note has no H1. Do not add it to new notes unless you are maintaining an older file.
- Store note type in the `type:` frontmatter field.
- Most notes live at the vault root as flat `.md` files. Type definitions are normal notes with `type: Type`; Tolaria creates new ones at the root and still reads legacy `type/` or `types/` folders. Saved views live in `views/`.
- Any frontmatter field containing [[wikilinks]] is treated as a relationship. Common names include `Belongs to:`, `Related to:`, `Workspace:`, and custom relationship names.
- Frontmatter properties that start with `_` are usually Tolaria-managed state. Leave them alone unless the user explicitly asks for them to change.

## Notes

```yaml
---
type: Project
status: Active
_icon: target
Workspace: "[[tolaria]]"
Belongs to:
  - "[[25q2]]"
Related to:
  - "[[person-luca-rossi]]"
aliases:
  - Tolaria work
url: https://example.com
---

# Ship Tolaria

Body content in Markdown.
```

## Types

Type definitions are regular notes. Use `type: Type` for new ones:

```yaml
---
type: Type
_icon: shapes
_color: blue
_sidebar_label: Projects
template: |
  ## Outcome

  ## Next actions
---

# Project
```

Useful type metadata includes `_icon`, `_color`, `_order`, `_sidebar_label`, `_pinned_properties`, `_list_properties_display`, `template`, `_sort`, `view`, and `visible`.

## Wikilinks

- [[filename]] or [[Note Title]] — link by filename or title
- [[filename|display text]] — with custom display text
- Works in frontmatter values and Markdown body

## Views

Saved views live in `views/*.yml` and are written as YAML:

```yaml
name: Active Projects
icon: kanban
color: blue
sort: modified:desc
filters:
  all:
    - field: type
      op: equals
      value: Project
    - field: status
      op: equals
      value: Active
```

## Filenames

Use kebab-case: `my-note-title.md`. One note per file.

## What agents should do

- Create and edit notes using the frontmatter and H1 conventions above.
- Create and edit type documents as regular notes with `type: Type`.
- Add or modify relationships without breaking existing wikilinks.
- Create and edit saved views in `views/`.
- Update `AGENTS.md` only when the user asks for vault-level guidance changes.

## What agents should avoid

- Do not infer a note's type from its folder; use the `type:` frontmatter field.
- Do not silently overwrite an existing custom `AGENTS.md`.
- Do not overwrite user-authored config or installation-specific app files unless the user explicitly asks.

# Git and AutoGit

Tolaria vaults have first-class, optional Git support. You retain control over when to create local history, connect a remote, commit, and push.

You can look at current changes and Git history from [[tolaria-bottom-bar]], create new commits and push them directly without ever leaving the app.

The manual commit dialog can draft a message from the changed files. Review and edit the draft before committing.

If you do not want to manage checkpoints manually, Tolaria also has an opt-in **AutoGit mode**. It creates conservative commits after an editing pause or when the app becomes inactive, then pushes when the vault has a configured remote.

![CleanShot 2026-04-17 at 17.44.08@2x.png](attachments/1776440668823-CleanShot_2026-04-17_at_17.44.08_2x.png)

You can enable AutoGit, choose whether it drafts messages with AI, and adjust its timing in Settings (`Cmd+,` or `Ctrl+,`).

Git also works when this vault is a folder inside a larger repository. Tolaria keeps app-created commits scoped to vault files, while pull and push still operate on the parent repository.

# Command Palette

One of [[tolaria-principles]] is being keyboard-first. Almost everything has shortcuts.

You can discover shortcuts from the app menus and from tooltips on buttons.

A lot of actions also have a fall back or a quick way to do them via the command palette, which you can open with `Cmd+K` (`Ctrl+K` on Windows and Linux)

You can really do almost everything with it, including navigating to sections, creating new notes of a certain type, switching the theme, exporting a note as PDF, or performing routine actions.

To jump straight to a note or file, use quick open with `Cmd+P` (`Ctrl+P` on Windows and Linux).

You don’t even need to find the exact keywords — the palette is smart enough to match a lot of commands semantically:

![CleanShot 2026-04-17 at 18.08.40@2x.png](attachments/1776442178567-CleanShot_2026-04-17_at_18.08.40_2x.png)

# Editor Playground

This note contains durable Markdown examples you can edit, select, move, collapse, and inspect in raw mode.

> [!NOTE] Rich in Tolaria, portable everywhere
> This callout stays a normal Markdown blockquote when another editor opens the file.

> [!TIP] Edit this callout
> Tolaria supports always-expanded callouts. Change the type or title in raw mode.

## A section to collapse

Move the pointer beside this heading and use its disclosure control. You can also press `Esc` to select the heading, then `Cmd+Enter` on macOS or `Ctrl+Enter` on Windows and Linux.

Everything until the next heading at the same or higher level belongs to the section. Collapsing it changes only the editor—not the Markdown.

### Try block selection

1. Put the cursor in this paragraph and press `Esc`.
2. Use the arrow keys to move the selected block.
3. Hold `Shift` while using the arrows to select more blocks.
4. Press `Enter` to edit text again.

Use `Cmd+Shift+Up` or `Cmd+Shift+Down` to move selected blocks on macOS. Use `Ctrl` instead of `Cmd` on Windows and Linux.

## Formatting that round-trips

This sentence contains ==Markdown highlight==. Select other text and press `Cmd+Shift+M` on macOS or `Ctrl+Shift+M` on Windows and Linux. Use the highlight color picker in the formatting toolbar to switch between yellow, green, red, blue, and purple.

- [ ] Press `Cmd+T` or `Ctrl+T` in a paragraph to turn it into a todo
- [ ] Type `/date` or `/time` to insert the current value

Create a code block with the slash menu, a triple-backtick fence, or `Cmd+Shift+Backtick` / `Ctrl+Shift+Backtick`:

```typescript
const vault = {
  format: "Markdown",
  history: "Git",
  lockedIn: false,
}
```

Use the language control to change syntax highlighting. Line numbers are editor presentation and never enter the file.

## Look underneath

Toggle raw mode with `Cmd+\` or `Ctrl+\`. The callouts, highlight, todos, and code block remain ordinary Markdown you can read with any editor.

# Get familiar with Tolaria

Use this checklist as a 15–20 minute tour of Tolaria. Every link opens a real file you can inspect, edit, and restore with Git.

`Cmd+click` on wikilinks to navigate 👇

- [ ] **Read the** [[tolaria-principles|Tolaria Principles]] — understand the core philosophy
- [ ] **Explore the** [[tolaria-sidebar]] — learn Inbox, All Notes, Archive, Favorites, Types, Folders
- [ ] **Browse the** [[tolaria-note-list]] — sorting, display properties, search within list
- [ ] **Try the** [[tolaria-editor|Editor]] and [[editor-playground]] — rich vs raw mode, callouts, blocks, code, highlights, whiteboards, PDF export, and collapsible sections
- [ ] **Open the** [[launch-plan-spreadsheet]] — values, formulas, wikilinks, formatting, and a cross-note property reference
- [ ] **Open the** [[project-dashboard]] — see a Markdown note render its own properties through a safe HTML block
- [ ] **Preview** [[sample-report.html]] — then toggle raw mode to inspect the standalone HTML source
- [ ] **Open the** [[the-properties-panel|Properties Panel]] — add a property, create a relationship
- [ ] **Try** [[tolaria-ai]] — choose an agent or direct model, understand permissions, and send a prompt with note context
- [ ] **Try the** [[command-palette]] — to do more from your keyboard
- [ ] **Check the** [[tolaria-bottom-bar]] and [[autogit]] — Git status, history, local commits, remotes, and optional checkpoints
- [ ] **Make it yours** in [[make-it-yours]] — theme, language, note width, and layout
- [ ] **Learn how to use** [[multiple-vaults]] — keep separate vaults open in one graph
- [ ] Mark this project as `status: done` when done

# Make It Yours

A few settings change how Tolaria looks and feels. Open Settings with `Cmd+,` or `Ctrl+,`.

### 🌗 Theme

Choose Light, Dark, or System. System follows your operating system's appearance as it changes. You can also switch the theme from the [[command-palette]].

### 🌍 Language

Tolaria's interface is available in more than 20 languages. By default it follows your system language when it's supported. Pick another one under Language in Settings. Missing translations fall back to English.

### 📏 Note width

Pick Normal for focused writing or Wide for tables, diagrams, and dense notes. Any single note can override the default from the editor toolbar.

### 🪟 Layout

Use `Cmd+1`, `Cmd+2`, and `Cmd+3` (`Ctrl` on Windows and Linux) to switch between the editor alone, the editor with the note list, and all panels.

# Multiple Vaults

Tolaria can manage more than one vault at the same time. This is useful when you want to keep separate folders or Git repositories, but still search and navigate across them as one knowledge graph.

To turn it on:

1. Open Settings.
2. Go to Vaults.
3. Enable `Use multiple vaults at the same time`.
4. Open the bottom-left vault menu.
5. Check the vaults you want to include in the unified graph.

Included vaults appear together in note lists, search, quick open, backlinks, and wikilink navigation. When a note could be ambiguous, Tolaria shows a small vault label so you know where it lives.

Each vault keeps its own files and Git repository. Commits, sync, saved views, folder navigation, and vault repair actions still belong to the selected vault. Use `Manage vaults` to rename vaults, choose colors, and set the default vault for new notes.

Cross-vault wikilinks use the target vault's stable alias when Tolaria needs one, such as `[[team/projects/alpha]]`. Links inside the same vault stay simple.

If you'd rather keep vaults completely separate, open one in its own window instead: use the bottom-left vault menu to open it in a new window. Each window works on its own vault.

# Properties Panel

The properties panel shows and edits a note's frontmatter in a user-friendly way.

### Type-Aware UI

Different property types render with appropriate controls:

- **Text and numbers** — simple input fields
- **Dates** — date picker for easy selection
- **Status** — dropdown with predefined options
- **Tags** — tag input with autocomplete

![CleanShot 2026-04-17 at 17.58.11@2x.png](attachments/1776441635173-CleanShot_2026-04-17_at_17.58.11_2x.png)

### Relationships

Wikilink values in frontmatter become clickable links to other notes. The panel shows relationships with a rich interface—click to navigate, see previews, and manage connections.

Tolaria also tracks backlinks and reverse relationships

![CleanShot 2026-04-17 at 18.01.19@2x.png](attachments/1776441716304-CleanShot_2026-04-17_at_18.01.19_2x.png)

### Default Relationships

Even if not in the frontmatter, you can add common relationships with one click. This is super opinionated and comes from my own experience. A lot of relationships between notes can simply be modelled as:

- ⬆️ **Belongs to** — Parent relationships
- ➡️ **Related to** — General connections
- ⬇️ **Has** — Child/possession relationships (inverse of belongs to)

These defaults help you quickly add structure without creating complex schemas and remembering property names that need to stay consistent across the vault.

# AI in Tolaria

Tolaria embraces AI without making it a requirement. Choose between coding agents that can work with vault files and direct models that answer from note context without file-editing tools.

### Coding agents

Tolaria can launch installed versions of Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Pi, Antigravity CLI, Kiro, and Hermes Agent.

Each agent owns its authentication and runtime. Tolaria gives it the active note and vault context, streams the conversation, and keeps file changes visible in the app.

Use **Vault Safe** for file, search, and edit work. Use **Power User** only when you intentionally want an agent to run supported shell commands inside the vault.

Agents that expose a reliable catalog can also show a model picker. Tolaria remembers model choices separately for each agent; **Agent default** lets the CLI choose.

### Direct models

Direct models are useful when you want chat over note context without giving the model vault-write tools. Tolaria supports local providers such as Ollama and LM Studio, hosted providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and OpenRouter, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

Provider credentials stay in local app configuration or an environment variable, not in this vault.

### Try it

1. Open the AI panel with `Cmd+Shift+L` or `Ctrl+Shift+L`.
2. Choose an installed coding agent or a configured direct model.
3. Ask: “Explain how [[project-dashboard]] gets its values.”
4. With a coding agent in Vault Safe mode, ask: “Add one unchecked learning task to [[get-familiar-with-tolaria]].”
5. Review the resulting file diff before you commit it.

Use the stop control if an agent takes the wrong direction.

### External tools

Because this vault contains `AGENTS.md`, an external AI tool can understand its file conventions even without Tolaria's built-in panel. Tolaria can also register its MCP server with supported tools such as Claude Code and Cursor, so they can search, read, create, update, and append notes, open a note in Tolaria, and list or attach vaults through vault-scoped operations.

# Bottom Bar

The bottom bar is Tolaria's status bar — more informational than interactive. It keeps you aware of your current state without getting in your way.

### 📂 Vault selection

By clicking on the vault bottom left you can change the active vault, open a vault in a new window, open a new local folder, create a new one by cloning a Git repo, or manage which vaults are included in your graph.

![CleanShot 2026-04-17 at 15.35.16@2x.png](attachments/1776432929539-CleanShot_2026-04-17_at_15.35.16_2x.png)

When `Use multiple vaults at the same time` is enabled in Settings → Vaults, this menu shows checkboxes for the vaults Tolaria should load together. Included vaults appear in search, note lists, quick open, backlinks, and wikilink navigation. The selected vault still controls repository-specific actions such as commits, sync, saved views, and folder navigation.

### 🔄 Git Sync Status

Shows pending uncommitted changes in your vault. When you see a count, you have uncommitted edits. Click to see what's changed or commit directly by clicking on `commit`.

The commit dialog can draft a message from your changes, and pushes when the vault has a remote. If you have [[autogit]] enabled, Tolaria creates these checkpoints for you automatically.

### ⚡ History

A lightweight git history view shows recent changes across all notes. See when notes were modified, by whom, and get quick access to change details.

![CleanShot 2026-04-17 at 15.32.38@2x.png](attachments/1776432798617-CleanShot_2026-04-17_at_15.32.38_2x.png)

### 🧮 App Version

The current Tolaria version. Useful when debugging or checking for new features.

### 🪄 AI Status

Shows which AI target is selected and whether an installed coding agent is available. Tolaria supports Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Pi, Antigravity CLI, Kiro, and Hermes Agent, plus configured direct models.

![CleanShot 2026-04-17 at 15.51.39@2x.png](attachments/1776433913782-CleanShot_2026-04-17_at_15.51.39_2x.png)

### 📣 Feedback

The Contribute button opens a small menu where you can report a bug, request features, join discussions, contribute code, or support Tolaria as a sponsor.

# Editor

The editor is where you write and edit your notes. Tolaria supports two modes:

### WYSIWYG Mode

The default experience. Similar to Notion — type naturally and see formatted output.

Supports slash commands for quick formatting, current date and time, live Markdown rendering, editable callouts, inline previews, drag and drop of images, collapsible sections, block selection, code blocks, Mermaid diagrams, math, sandboxed HTML blocks, colored highlights, and more.

Open [[editor-playground]] for examples you can manipulate directly.

- List **item** 1
  - Nested *italic item*
1. **Numbered item** in bold
2. Numbered second item

> Quote from a wise author

- [ ] Task 1
- [ ] Task 2

```javascript
(param) => (return 3*2) /* code block */
```

### Raw Mode

Shows the actual file characters. Access it with `Cmd+\` or `Ctrl+\`, or use the source button in the breadcrumb bar. It is useful when you need precise control over Markdown or YAML frontmatter.

Invalid YAML frontmatter is highlighted so structural mistakes are easier to locate.

### Filename Display

The note's filename is always visible at the top of the editor. This keeps you aware of how the note will be named and linked.

### H1-to-Filename Sync

When you create a new untitled note, the first H1 heading automatically sets its filename as soon as it becomes a real title. After that, the filename stays put until you rename it yourself from the breadcrumb bar or the note list.

You can turn this off in Settings → Titles & Filenames (`Cmd+,` or `Ctrl+,`).

### Wikilinks

Type `[[` to trigger autocomplete from your entire vault. This creates links to other notes, enabling the knowledge graph.

Wikilinks also auto-update if the filename changes. If a wikilink points to a note that doesn't exist yet, you can create that note straight from the link.

![BlockNote image](attachments/1776508281809-CleanShot_2026-04-18_at_12.30.44_2x.png)

### Breadcrumb Bar Actions

The breadcrumb bar (above the editor) is the hub for note-level actions: favoriting, marking organized, switching editor modes, viewing git diff, and accessing properties.

### Whiteboards

Notes can contain tldraw whiteboards for sketches and diagrams. The board is still stored in the Markdown file, so it lives in the vault and is versioned by Git like everything else. Expand a board to work on it full screen.

### Export as PDF

Use the export button in the editor toolbar, or run `Export note as PDF` from the [[command-palette]], to turn the current note into a PDF.

# Note List

The note list shows the subset of notes selected by the current sidebar section. For example, clicking "Types → Project" shows all your Project notes.

### ⬇️ Sorting

You can sort the note list by any note property (they get dynamically loaded from the notes), plus file properties like modified and creation time.

Your choice will be remembered for that specific section.

![CleanShot 2026-04-16 at 21.58.56@2x.png](attachments/1776369547761-CleanShot_2026-04-16_at_21.58.56_2x.png)

### 💅 Display Properties

You can customize which properties appear as columns in the note list. This lets you see important metadata at a glance without opening individual notes.

![CleanShot 2026-04-16 at 21.56.07@2x.png](attachments/1776369416105-CleanShot_2026-04-16_at_21.56.07_2x.png)

For properties that are URLs or other notes, you can open them directly from the note list with `Cmd+click` (`Ctrl+click` on Windows and Linux)

### 🔍 Search

You can perform instant keyword search within the current list of notes to filter down to what you need. This searches across all the notes content.

### 🧭 Neighborhood mode

Neighborhood mode pivots the note list around one note instead of a whole section. The selected note stays pinned at the top, and the rest of the list reorganizes into groups based on the note’s relationships with other notes.

Use it when you want to move through related projects, people, or topics without jumping back to the sidebar. To enter Neighborhood mode, `Cmd+click` a note in the list, focus a note and press `Cmd+Enter` (use `Ctrl` on Windows and Linux), or use the neighborhood button in the editor toolbar. You can use `Esc` to go back to the previous neighborhood, or to leave the mode altogether

![CleanShot 2026-04-20 at 10.17.53@2x.png](attachments/1776673161755-CleanShot_2026-04-20_at_10.17.53_2x.png)

### ➕ Creating notes

The + button in the note list creates a new note of the current type. If you're viewing a type-filtered section, the new note automatically gets that type.

You can also create a new note anywhere with `Cmd+N` (`Ctrl+N` on Windows and Linux) or from the [[command-palette]]

# Principles

Tolaria is built on a few core principles that guide our design decisions:

### 📑 Files-first

Your notes are plain markdown files. They're portable, work with any editor, and require no export step. Your data belongs to you, not to any app.

### 🔌 Git-first

Git is Tolaria's recommended history and sync layer, not a requirement. A plain Markdown folder works as a vault; enabling Git adds diffs, local history, recovery, remotes, and multi-device sync without depending on Tolaria servers.

### 🛜 Offline-first, zero lock-in

No accounts, no subscriptions, no cloud dependencies. Your vault works completely offline and always will. If you stop using Tolaria, you lose nothing.

### 🔬 Open source

Tolaria is free and [open source](https://github.com/refactoringhq/tolaria). I built this for myself ([[luca-rossi]]) and for sharing it with others.

### 📋 Standards-based

Notes are markdown files with YAML frontmatter. No proprietary formats, no locked-in data. Everything works with standard tools if you decide to move away from Tolaria.

### 🔍 Types as lenses — not schemas

Types in Tolaria are navigation aids, not enforcement mechanisms. There's no required fields, no validation, just helpful categories for finding notes.

### 🪄AI-first — but not AI-only

A vault of files works very well with AI agents, but you are free to use whatever you want. Tolaria supports several local coding agents plus direct local and API models. The vault's `AGENTS.md` explains its conventions to external tools without making AI a prerequisite.

### ⌨️ Keyboard-first

Tolaria is designed for power-users who want to use keyboard as much as possible. A lot of how we designed [[tolaria-editor]] and [[command-palette]] is based on this.

### 💪 Built from real use

Tolaria was created to manage my personal vault of 10,000+ notes, and I use it every day. Every feature exists because it solved a real problem.

# Sidebar

The sidebar is your primary navigation tool. It groups notes in different ways so you can find what you need quickly.

### 📥 Inbox

Notes that aren't *organized* yet.

This is inspired by [Tiago Forte](https://www.buildingasecondbrain.com/)'s concept of separating capture from organize. An “organized” note is a note that you know what you will do with. It may belong to a project, to a responsibility, a topic, or any concept related to how you organize work.

Review your inbox (e.g.) weekly to keep it from growing too large. You can disable the Inbox in Settings (`Cmd+,` or `Ctrl+,`) if you don’t like this workflow.

You can flag a note as *organized* by clicking on the “circle task” icon in the breadcrumbs bar, or with `Cmd+E` (`Ctrl+E` on Windows and Linux).

### 🗃️ All Notes

As the name suggests, that’s the entire vault — every single note.

### 📦 Archive

A permanent home for notes you don't want to delete but don't want to see regularly. Archive aggressively to keep your vault clean. Archived notes still appear in search results, but not in sidebar sections.

### ⭐ Favorites

Notes you've manually pinned to keep them top-of-mind. Great for active projects, journal entries, or reference notes you access frequently.

You can reorder them by dragging them in the sidebar.

Toggle a favorite note from the ⭐ button in the breadcrumbs bar, or with `Cmd+D` (`Ctrl+D` on Windows and Linux).

### 🔍 Views

You can create custom views that filter notes by complex, nested criteria. The view editor fetches all available properties, plus allows for some tricks (like regexes and natural language dates)

![CleanShot 2026-04-16 at 22.02.51@2x.png](attachments/1776369786040-CleanShot_2026-04-16_at_22.02.51_2x.png)

Views are simple yaml files that get stored in the views folder (e.g. [[views/active-projects.yml]]). They can be edited easily and even created by the AI 👇

```yaml
name: Active Projects
icon: 🚀
filters:
  all:
  - field: type
    op: equals
    value: Project
  - field: Status
    op: equals
    value: Active
  - any:
    - field: status
      op: equals
      value: active
    - field: date
      op: after
      value: in 1 week
```

### 🧩 Types

The main organizational device in Tolaria. Each note has a type, which by default is [[note]].

Each type can have its own icon and color, which you can change by right-clicking on it in the sidebar, or manually changing it in the properties or frontmatter of the type file.

Types are simply stored as markdown files, like [[topic]], or [[project]].

Click any type on the sidebar to see all notes of that type in the note list.

### 📂 Folders

Tolaria stores notes in the root of the vault by default, but also scans your vault’s folder structure, which you can navigate at the bottom of the sidebar.

Folders are listed last because they are a secondary organization method—not the primary one.

### 🗑️ Trash

There is no trash bin: when you delete a note (`Cmd+Backspace` or `Ctrl+Backspace`), it’s gone — but your git history is your safety net. You can always recover deleted notes from git if needed.
